analysis:
The PR is docs-only (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/architecture/inference.md). It adds provider-local startup calibration. Described behavior is a one-token health check marked EngineMeasurementPurpose.startupWarmup, and a 128-token warmup plus two uncached solo probes (<=512 prompt tokens, <=32 output tokens). It also adds a foreground lease (IdleCalibrationCoordinator.beginForeground) that cancels calibration when a customer request arrives. Calibration runs one session at a time per Mac and waits for actual stream retirement (EngineV2.submitWithRetirement) before customer admission. The docs say the memory floors, concurrency ceilings, activation and OS reserves, deadlines, and capacity wire fields are unchanged.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-041/A-001: calibration probes are uncached, so they should not feed the SSD prefix-cache. This is stated in the docs but is not verifiable from docs alone. Synthetic calibration prompts are not claimed to donate to the encrypted SSD cache, so the at-rest surface is not shown to widen.
- T-007/T-010: calibration output reaches the coordinator through existing capacity heartbeats. A malicious provider (ADV-001) can already self-report capacity. Calibration is local and unattested, so this is not a new trust assumption.
- T-010 (cancellation): foreground cancellation of calibration is described.
- T-029 (idle GPU): calibration gates on an idle Mac, nominal thermal state, and no Low Power Mode.

The actual code (ProviderLoop+ModelCalibration.swift, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration.swift, IdleCalibrationCoordinator.swift) is not in this batch. Later passes should verify there that probes bypass the prefix-cache donation path, use no consumer data, and do not count toward served-request, output-token or billing counters. No security regression is evident from the documentation changes.
